title: Holmes 2020 · 2IFC tactile calibration
citation: Holmes, N. P., Martin, D. J., Mitchell, W., Noorani, Z., & Thorne, A. (2020). Do sounds near the hand facilitate tactile reaction times? Four experiments and a meta-analysis provide mixed support and suggest a small effect size. Experimental Brain Research, 238, 995–1009.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

reference_parameters.planner_scope: The source settings describe this companion procedure. The Planner contains no executable trial schedule for it.

published_method.scope: The independent threshold-setting session before the speeded near/far hand tasks.
published_method.procedure: Deliver a 125 ms vibration during one of the two LED-marked intervals under continuous masking noise. The participant presses the corresponding first/second button. Two flashes from both LEDs follow an incorrect or omitted answer; repeat omissions.
published_method.apparatus: Oticon bone-conducting vibrator held between index finger and thumb, near-80 dB white-noise masking and two red interval LEDs. The separate unmasked strong-target check sets the working comparison at 1.5 times the weak command level.

stimulus_type.value: Continuous auditory white noise mask, with LED interval markers and one vibration.
stimulus_type.source: Journal pp. 997–998, Experiment 1; shared apparatus and procedure

implementation_gaps: Requires a two-interval visual and tactile scheduler, calibrated continuous masking and a response-dependent QUEST loop with omission repeats.
Actual waveform and drive transfer, nominal-to-physical intensity mapping, thresholds and trainee-specific repeated sequences are unresolved.
